story.title: A Letter to Uncle Jim

story.goalShort: I want to keep Washington from betting the country on a hydrogen bomb.

facts: I sat down after the briefing and wrote Jim a long letter.
I admitted that when we last spoke, "I was inclined to think that the super might also be relevant."
I told him that technically it was still "a weapon of unknown design, cost, deliverability and military value," and that only the climate of opinion had changed.
I wrote Jim that "two experienced promoters have been at work, i.e. Ernest Lawrence and Edward Teller."
I told him what really worried me: the thing had caught the imagination of congressional and military people as the answer to the Russian advance.
I wrote that "it would be folly to oppose the exploration of this weapon," but that becoming committed to it as the way to save the country and the peace "appears to me full of dangers."
I added that the Joint Chiefs were leaning toward asking the president for a crash program, and that even Hans was thinking of returning to Los Alamos full time.
Hans arrived in the afternoon with Edward, who was already going around the country recruiting.
Edward spoke as though Hans had already said he would come; Hans said he'd come for my advice.
I didn't give him the advice he was hoping for. I was as undecided and as troubled as he was.
I said little about my own views on the Super.
I did tell them that Jim was opposed to a crash program.
Edward seemed to leave delighted, as if I were sitting on the fence, and still hoping Hans would join him at Los Alamos.
